summary_oneline: Add a shared, event-sourced SDD ledger that preserves discovered work and provenance across linked worktrees.

localization.role: Existing async resolver from a linked worktree to the main checkout plane.
Resolves local or absolute wiki storage directories.
SQLite page, edge, FTS, neighbor and audit contract reusable by a ledger index.
Read federation and qualified identifier behavior for a separate ledger plane.
Current durable-memory write surface with an asserted link.
Task readiness, worktree provisioning and in-progress lifecycle command.

constraints.statement: Worktree plane resolution is already implemented as an async read consumer outside the wiki project package.
constraints.implication: The ledger should reuse or deliberately promote this seam rather than introduce a second incompatible common-directory algorithm.

constraints.statement: SQLite wiki writes run through per-call connections and migrations commit an UPDATE on every normal connection; the inspected store has no busy-timeout or explicit immediate transaction configuration.
constraints.implication: A concurrency spike must set and test the ledger's durability and claim semantics before SDD command integration.

constraints.statement: Federation fans out reads while reserving writes for the local plane or an explicitly opened namespace store.
constraints.implication: Ledger reads can federate, but ledger writes require a direct, explicit target.

constraints.statement: The current remember input has only an optional link and relation, and the managed hook only renders a post-commit refresh.
constraints.implication: Provenance fields and post-merge refresh must be specified as compatibility-sensitive API and installer changes.

constraints.statement: SDD lifecycle state is index-driven, while reports and deferred findings are not mandatory records.
constraints.implication: The ledger can fill a real gap, but all affected SDD platform command twins need an explicit rollout scope.

new: A shared event log and rebuildable ledger index rooted at the main checkout.
Ledger command and tool surfaces for discovered work, claims, closures, provenance and scoped context.
modified: Worktree plane resolution, SQLite configuration, federation registration, wiki memory inputs, managed hooks and SDD lifecycle commands.
untouched: Provider clients and unrelated agent execution behavior.
Replacing the existing wiki retrieval plane or requiring a server-backed tracker in v1.
patterns: Reuse `SQLiteWikiStore` page-edge contracts and `FederatedWikiStore` read behavior.
risks: A separate plane must have a direct write target because federation is deliberately read-oriented.
Shared-root code duplicated across packages can diverge unless a single API owner is selected.
Concurrent append and index updates need empirical validation before they become an agent workflow requirement.

confidence_map.statement: A linked worktree can resolve the main checkout's existing wiki plane through `resolve_plane_root`.
confidence_map.reasoning: Direct source read confirms the git-common-directory algorithm.

confidence_map.statement: The SQLite wiki store can represent ledger pages, provenance-bearing edges, lexical search, adjacency and dangling-edge audits.
confidence_map.reasoning: Direct source reads cover all named primitives.

confidence_map.statement: The current SQLite configuration needs a dedicated concurrent-writer spike before it can underpin atomic ledger claims.
confidence_map.reasoning: The inspected implementation lacks the proposed controls, but no load test was run.

confidence_map.statement: A separate ledger plane can be exposed through existing federation reads.
confidence_map.reasoning: The read path is direct; the proposed ledger write and cross-plane lifecycle contract remains design work.

confidence_map.statement: The proposed workflow integration targets real gaps in current review, readiness and completion commands.
confidence_map.reasoning: The current command documents directly show the relevant state transitions and optional review persistence.

recommended_next_command.rationale: The user resolved the deployment, provenance and rollout decisions; specification work can now formalize the concurrency spike and interface contracts.

meta.notes: Research was not truncated. The user selected single-host shared-worktree v1, general-purpose provenance support, and all three platform command twins. The plan-schema omission of wiki query types was handled by persisting wiki orientation separately.
